newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM platinum group metals end mixed, gold rises.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM platinum group metals end mixed, gold rises.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Friday, with gold rising on the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar while platinum group metals (PGMs) were mixed, Japanese traders said.
In palladium, spot June ended sharply higher reflecting tightness in near-term supplies, while other contracts were lower on fresh selling.
"Although there have been no signs that Russia has resumed PGM sales in the spot market, there is a perception that TOCOM palladium prices have reached their ceiling," one trader said.
Benchmark April palladium closed six yen weaker at 529 yen.
Traders said private investors were building fresh shorts in distant months of palladium.
In gold futures, private investors were keen to sell gold futures to take profits, while trade houses bought gold futures while selling spot gold in arbitrage dealings, they said.
Gold futures ranged from 12 yen to 17 yen per gram up. Benchmark April ended 17 yen up at 1,248 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $340.05/35 per ounce at 0740 GMT, against $340.20/70 in New York on Thursday.
Focus is on whether the Group of Seven nations's summit starting later today, will impact the currency market.

Platinum futures ended mixed. Strength in spot platinum helped push up TOCOM spot June while distant months were lower in anticipation that prices will be heading lower later this year, the traders said.

"Concern over the protracted delay in PGM shipments caused dollar-based PGM prices to rise in speculative trade," one trader said. "But the domestic platinum market is not as tight as the palladium market," he said. Platinum prices ranged from 11 yen per gram lower to 21 yen up. Benchmark April platinum ended 11 yen down at 1,357 yen. Benchmark April silver closed 3.1 yen per 10 grams higher at 177.3 yen.
